hook.text: Hospital infections kill 100,000 Americans yearly — many start on implant surfaces where bacteria form biofilms.

buildup.text: Bacteria colonize implant surfaces within hours — forming biofilms that antibiotics cannot penetrate.

discovery.text: Silver nanoparticle coatings release Ag⁺ ions that kill bacteria on contact — a centuries-old strategy modernized.

twist.text: Too much silver kills human cells too — the therapeutic window between killing bacteria and harming tissue is narrow.

climax.text: Nano-textured surfaces mimic cicada wings — tiny pillars physically rupture bacteria without any chemicals at all.

punchline.text: Surfaces that kill bacteria on contact — fighting infection at the front line.

quiz.question: How do nano-textured antimicrobial surfaces work?
options: They release antibiotic drugs over time
Tiny physical pillars mechanically rupture bacterial cell membranes
They heat up to kill bacteria thermally
